key_insight: DADiff uses a diffusion model to quantify source-target dynamics mismatch via generative trajectory deviation, then adapts policies with either reward modification or data selection.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical way to transfer reinforcement learning policies to new operating conditions when only limited target-domain interaction data is available.
method: Train a diffusion-based next-state generator on source dynamics.
Compare source vs. target generative trajectories to estimate mismatch.
Use the mismatch signal for reward shaping or filtering data to adapt policy training.
evidence_signal: The paper reports extensive experiments across environments with different shifts, and the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in handling dynamics mismatch.
watch_item: Effectiveness may depend on how well the diffusion model captures transition dynamics and on the quality of limited target-domain samples used for adaptation.
paper_title: DADiff: Diffusion-Driven Cross-Domain Policy Adaptation for Reinforcement Learning
